# Minimal Viable Hardware Configuration

Dimension covering K3s resource floor, Docker overhead, OPA costs, combined
stack estimates, and homelab hardware viability.

## K3s Resource Floor (Official Profiling)

From K3s v1.26.5, 95th percentile, steady-state [24]:

| Configuration | CPU | RAM | Disk |
|--------------|-----|-----|------|
| Server + workload (Intel 8375C) | 6% (~0.17 cores) | 1596 MB | 10 IOPS, 500 KiB/s, <10ms [24] |
| Server + workload (Pi4B) | 30% | 1588 MB | 10 IOPS, 500 KiB/s, <10ms [24] |
| Agent (Intel 8375C) | 3% (~0.09 cores) | 275 MB | minimal [24] |
| Agent (Pi4B) | 10% | 268 MB | minimal [24] |

Official minimums [23]:
- Server node: **2 cores, 2 GB RAM**
- Agent node: **1 core, 512 MB RAM**

Agent joining produces "~20% CPU spikes over baseline" [24].

### Disk Requirements

- Kine/SQLite: **10 IOPS, 500 KiB/sec, <10ms latency** [24]
- Embedded etcd: **50 IOPS, 250 KiB/sec, <5ms latency** [24]
- "SD cards and eMMC cannot handle the IO load" — external SSDs required for
  Raspberry Pi [23]
- SSD strongly recommended for all deployments [23]

## Docker Overhead

Docker standalone on 1 GB Ubuntu VM: **216 MB** RAM (vs 167 MB base OS) —
Docker itself adds ~49 MB [25]. Negligible.

## OPA Evaluation Costs

RBAC benchmark (Go reference implementation) [26]:
- **45032 ns/op (~45 µs)** average latency
- **20977 B/op (~21 KB)** memory per evaluation
- 27295 samples

Linear fragment optimization enables "near constant time" evaluation [26].

**Caveat**: OpenShell uses regorus (Rust Rego evaluator), not Go OPA [26].
No regorus benchmarks found. Rust implementations are typically faster than
Go for CPU-bound work, but this is inference, not data.

## OpenShell-Specific Overhead

**No profiling data exists** for OpenShell's gateway and cluster containers.
The architecture describes two main containers [6]. Estimated 300-800 MB
additional RAM based on typical Go/Rust services (est.).

## Combined Stack Estimate

| Component | CPU | RAM | Disk |
|-----------|-----|-----|------|
| K3s server (SQLite, steady-state) | 6% of host CPU [24] | 1596 MB [24] | 10 IOPS [24] |
| Docker engine | negligible | ~49 MB [25] | ~1 GB images (est.) |
| OPA/regorus per evaluation | ~45 µs [26] | ~21 KB [26] | N/A |
| OpenShell (gateway + cluster) | **unknown** | **300-800 MB (est.)** | **unknown** |
| **Estimated combined floor** | **~0.5 cores (est.)** | **~2.0-2.5 GB (est.)** | **SSD, ~10 GB (est.)** |

## GPU Requirements

**None required for Claude Code + Anthropic API.** The privacy router routes
to "frontier models (Claude, GPT) only when policy permits" [8]. GPU hardware
(GB300, DGX Spark) is for local inference with models like Nemotron [19] — not
for the sandbox/policy layer.

Anthropic-compatible inference routing: POST /v1/messages [7]. No local compute
required.

## Homelab Hardware Viability

| Hardware | Typical Specs | Viable? | Notes |
|----------|-------------|---------|-------|
| Intel NUC (11/12 gen) | i5/i7, 16-32 GB, NVMe | **Yes** | Exceeds all requirements. Ideal candidate. |
| Intel NUC (8th gen) | i3/i5, 8-16 GB, SATA SSD | **Yes** | 8 GB marginal; 16 GB comfortable. |
| Old laptop (2018+) | i5/i7, 8-16 GB, SSD | **Likely yes** | SSD required. 8 GB is tight. |
| Old laptop (pre-2018) | i5, 4-8 GB, HDD | **Marginal** | HDD likely fails IOPS. 4 GB insufficient. |
| Raspberry Pi 5 | Cortex-A76, 8 GB, ext SSD | **Marginal** | 8 GB model only. External SSD mandatory [23]. Pi4B profiling shows 30% CPU for K3s server [24]; Pi 5 is faster but no direct data (est.). |
| Raspberry Pi 4 | Cortex-A72, 2-8 GB | **Unlikely** | 2-4 GB insufficient. 8 GB possible with ext SSD. 30% CPU baseline [24]. |
| SFF PC (Optiplex, ThinkCentre) | i5/i7, 8-32 GB, SSD | **Yes** | Equivalent to NUC assessment. |

### Portainer Findings on Constrained Hardware

On 1 GB RAM VMs [25]:
- K3s idle: 750 MB
- After deploying workload: API server timeouts
- "None of the lightweight Kubernetes distributions seem suitable for 1 GB RAM
  devices with actual workloads" [25]
- Master node requires at least 2 GB RAM [25]

### K3s Resource Optimization

K3s overhead can be reduced 30-40% by disabling unused components (Traefik,
ServiceLB, metrics-server) [from discovery agent — optimization guide, unverified].

## Gaps and Limitations

- OpenShell's own resource consumption is the largest sizing unknown
- K3s profiling used v1.26.5 — newer versions may differ [24]
- Intel 8375C is a server CPU — laptop percentages will be higher [24]
- No data on memory behavior under heavy agent workloads (many tool calls/sec)
- Container image sizes not reported — affects disk budget and pull times
- Swap performance impact with <8 GB RAM is undocumented
